# onetsolutions_hosting_email_account (Resource)

Manages a mailbox of a web hosting.

!> **Destroying deletes the messages.** Destroying the resource, or a change that replaces it
(`email`, `hosting_id`), deletes the mailbox and every message in it; `terraform plan` warns
before it does. `deletion_protection = true` refuses the destroy.

## Password and quota

`password` and `quota_mb` change in place. The password is never read back: it is kept in the
state (marked sensitive) and an import cannot recover it, so the first apply after an import sets
the mailbox's password to the configured one, with a plan-time warning. A quota changed outside
Terraform shows as a difference and is set back.

## Main mailbox

The web hosting's main mailbox, `<username>@<domain>`, belongs to the hosting account: it can be
neither created nor deleted, but it can be imported to manage its password and quota (`is_main` is
then `true`). Without `quota_mb` in its configuration, its quota is left as it is. Destroying it
only removes it from the state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_web_hosting" "site" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

variable "mailbox_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "onetsolutions_hosting_email_account" "contact" {
  hosting_id = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  email      = "contact@example.com"
  password   = var.mailbox_password
  quota_mb   = 1024
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) The address of the mailbox, in lowercase, on a domain of the web hosting, such as `contact@example.com`. Changing it recreates the mailbox, which deletes its messages.
- `hosting_id` (String) The UUID of the web hosting. Changing it recreates the object in the other web hosting.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The password of the mailbox. Can be changed in place; after an import, the next apply sets the mailbox's password to the configured one. At least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a special character. It is never read back: it is stored in the state, and an import cannot recover it.

### Optional

- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether destroying (or replacing) the mailbox is refused. Defaults to `false`. Set it to `false` and apply before destroying a protected mailbox.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `quota_mb` (Number) The disk quota of the mailbox in MB; `0` means unlimited. Defaults to `250`, except for the main mailbox, whose quota is then left as it is. Can be changed in place.

### Read-Only

- `domain` (String) The domain of the address.
- `id` (String) The address of the mailbox, the same as `email`.
- `is_main` (Boolean) Whether this is the web hosting's main mailbox, which belongs to the hosting account: it can be imported to manage its password and quota, and destroying it only removes it from the state.
- `user` (String) The login of the mailbox.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_hosting_email_account.contact
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/5e7c2a1b-9d3f-4a6e-8b2c-1d0f9e8a7b6c/contact@example.com"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<hosting_id>/<email>, or <hosting_id>/<email> when the provider sets
# organization_id and project_id. The password cannot be imported: the next apply sets the configured one.
terraform import onetsolutions_hosting_email_account.contact 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/5e7c2a1b-9d3f-4a6e-8b2c-1d0f9e8a7b6c/contact@example.com
```
